variants.title: The raccoon babies are coming down for dinner
variants.body: Mom goes first. The kits follow, one tiny paw at a time, and somebody always slips the last bit. (They're fine. Mostly embarrassed.)

variants.title: Raccoon family, now leaving the tree
variants.body: Mom, then a wobbly line of kits. They regroup at the bottom, sniff the air, and head out {place} like a very small parade.

variants.title: The kits are practicing tree-climbing in reverse
variants.body: Down is harder than up. Lots of hugging the trunk. Mom waits at the bottom, not impressed, not worried.

variants.title: The raccoon kits are heading out for their first rounds
variants.body: Mom shimmies down the trunk and waits while the kits figure it out, one wobbly paw at a time. Tonight's lesson: the quiet way along {street} toward {green}, where the snacks are.

variants.title: A raccoon is doing the nightly rounds
variants.body: Same route as yesterday: the can with the loose lid, then the one by the fence. Raccoons never forget a good lid.

variants.title: The night shift has clocked in
variants.body: Somewhere {place}, a raccoon is patting along the curb with those clever little hands, reading the block by touch.

variants.title: A raccoon is investigating a very interesting lid
variants.body: Pry, wiggle, think, try again. Raccoons are excellent at puzzles, especially the ones you didn't mean to set.

variants.title: A raccoon is walking the same route as always
variants.body: Down {street}, a careful pat along the curb, a peek behind {landmark}, then on toward {green}. They've done this loop so many nights they could do it with their eyes closed.

variants.title: A raccoon is splashing a snack around
variants.body: Rolling it between wet paws. They aren't washing it, exactly: wet paws just feel things better. Very fancy.

variants.title: Raccoon at the puddle, hands busy
variants.body: Dabble, dabble, squint. Those front paws are so sensitive they're basically doing the looking.

variants.title: A raccoon found a puddle near {green}
variants.body: They're sitting at the edge, rolling something between wet paws, totally absorbed. It looks like washing. It's really feeling: wet fingers tell them more about what they've got.

variants.title: A raccoon is on a winter-prep snack tour
variants.body: Acorns, fallen apples, a dropped slice of pizza. Fall is all-you-can-eat season, and they take it very seriously.

variants.title: Raccoon, getting extra fluffy for winter
variants.body: Every snack {place} is going straight to the winter-coat fund. Chubby is the goal.

variants.title: A raccoon is on a serious fall snack mission
variants.body: Fallen apples, acorns, whatever the trees around {green} dropped today. Every bite goes toward a cozy winter, and they are not skipping a single one.

variants.title: The raccoons called in cozy
variants.body: Too cold to bother. They're curled up in the den, tails over noses, waiting for a nicer night.

variants.title: A raccoon peeks out, then nopes back in
variants.body: On freezing nights they'll skip a shift or two. The trash cans {place} can wait.

variants.title: The raccoons are sleeping in tonight
variants.body: Somewhere in a hollow tree near {green}, a raccoon family is piled into one warm, stripy heap. The cans on {street} will still be there when it's warmer.

variants.title: A raccoon mom is sneaking out for a quick bite
variants.body: Her kits are tucked in a den up high. She'll grab a snack and be back before anyone wakes up.

variants.title: Raccoon mom, on a very short break
variants.body: Babies at home, snacks out here. She moves fast, eats faster, and heads straight back.

variants.title: A raccoon mom just slipped out for a minute
variants.body: Her kits are tucked in a den high above {street}, too little to follow. She'll grab a quick bite near {green} and hurry right back to the pile.

variants.title: An opossum is tightrope-walking the fence
variants.body: Slow and steady, tail helping with the balance. They're on bug and slug patrol {place}, and they're in no rush.

variants.title: An opossum is out on a snack walk
variants.body: Fallen fruit, beetles, the odd snail. They tidy up the block and ask for nothing in return. Model neighbor.

variants.title: A little white face is moving along the fence
variants.body: That's an opossum, waddling through. Pink nose, round ears, zero hurry.

variants.title: An opossum is taking the scenic route
variants.body: Along the fences behind {street}, slow and steady, nose working the whole way. They're eating slugs and fallen fruit and asking nothing of anyone. Honestly, a perfect neighbor.

variants.title: An opossum mom has passengers tonight
variants.body: A row of babies clings to her back, holding on tight while she waddles along. Best bus in town.

variants.title: Opossum mom, giving piggyback rides
variants.body: When the babies get too big for her pouch, they ride on top instead. Nobody gets left behind.

variants.title: An opossum mom is giving the whole family a ride
variants.body: A row of tiny babies clings to her back as she waddles along the edge of {green}. When one slips, she waits. Nobody gets left behind on this bus.

variants.title: A young opossum is out on their own for the first time
variants.body: Everything is new: the curb, the hedge, the smell of the gardens {place}. They sniff all of it. Twice.

variants.title: A teenage opossum is exploring
variants.body: Fresh out of mom's care and very curious. Every flowerpot needs a careful sniff.

variants.title: A young opossum is out exploring for the very first time
variants.body: New to being on their own, they're giving every flowerpot near {street} a careful, curious sniff. Everything is interesting. Everything takes a while.

variants.title: The opossums are keeping their ears warm
variants.body: Bare ears and tails don't love the cold. Tonight they're staying tucked in somewhere snug.

variants.title: Opossum, staying in under a pile of leaves
variants.body: Too chilly for a walk. They'll pop out again on a milder night.

variants.title: The opossums are waiting out the cold
variants.body: Bare pink ears and tails don't love winter, so tonight they're curled up somewhere snug near {green}, under leaves or tucked beneath a porch.

variants.title: The moths are having a dance party at the streetlight
variants.body: They steer by keeping the brightest light above them, so a streetlight sends them spinning. Every porch light switched off {place} helps them home.

variants.title: A little crowd is circling the lamp
variants.body: Fuzzy wings, feathery antennae, dizzy loops. Look closely: some are as fancy as butterflies, just on the night shift.

variants.title: The moths found the streetlight again
variants.body: Round and round they go. It's not a party they meant to join, and a dark porch lets them get back to their night.

variants.title: The moths have found the streetlight on {street}
variants.body: Round and round they go, dizzy and determined, steering by a light that isn't the moon. Every window that goes dark nearby helps one of them get back to their night.

variants.title: The moths are covering the late shift at the flowers
variants.body: While the bees sleep, moths sip nectar and carry pollen from bloom to bloom. Very underrated coworkers.

variants.title: A moth is sipping from a night flower
variants.body: Fuzzy, quiet and secretly doing important work. The garden {place} has a night crew.

variants.title: The night-shift pollinators are working {green}
variants.body: While the bees sleep, moths drift from bloom to bloom in the dark, sipping and carrying pollen. Most people never see them. The flowers know.

variants.title: The last moths of the year are fluttering by
variants.body: On mild fall evenings a few are still out. Many will spend winter as cocoons tucked in fallen leaves.

variants.title: One brave fall moth is out tonight
variants.body: Most are already bundled up as cocoons in the leaf litter. This one wanted one more evening.

variants.title: One of the year's last moths is out over {green}
variants.body: On a mild fall evening, a single moth flutters by, unhurried. Most of their friends are already tucked into the leaf litter as cocoons, waiting for spring.

variants.title: The pigeons are heading out for breakfast
variants.body: They leave the ledge in little groups and drop onto the sidewalk {place}, checking where crumbs landed last night.

variants.title: First flight of the morning
variants.body: A clap of wings, a loop around the block, and down they come to see what the day left out.

variants.title: The pigeons are doing their morning crumb inspection
variants.body: Strut, peck, strut. Every inch of sidewalk gets a very official review.

variants.title: The pigeons are heading out for breakfast on {street}
variants.body: They lift off the ledges in little flocks, loop once around {landmark}, and land wherever the morning left crumbs. Same breakfast spots, same friends, every day.

variants.title: A pigeon is sunbathing like it's a beach day
variants.body: One wing tipped up, eyes half closed. The warmth shakes out parasites, and honestly it just feels nice.

variants.title: A pigeon is lying flat on a warm ledge
variants.body: Feathers fluffed, wing out, fully melted. Do not disturb.

variants.title: A pigeon is soaking up the sun near {landmark}
variants.body: One wing tipped open, eyes half closed, flattened out on a warm ledge. The heat helps their feathers. Mostly, it just feels really, really nice.

variants.title: A pigeon is showing off his best moves
variants.body: He puffs up, spins in a circle and bows, cooing the whole time. She keeps eating like she hasn't noticed. She noticed.

variants.title: Pigeon romance is happening on the sidewalk
variants.body: Puff, spin, bow, coo. Repeat. Pairs often stay together for life, so the routine has to be good.

variants.title: Pigeon romance is happening on {street}
variants.body: He puffs up his shiny neck, spins in a circle and bows, cooing his heart out. She pretends to keep eating. Pigeon pairs often stay together for life, so she's taking her time deciding.

variants.title: A pigeon is carrying one extremely important twig
variants.body: City pigeons nest any time of year. That twig is headed to a ledge {place}, maybe one you walk under every day.

variants.title: Pigeon, busy with home improvements
variants.body: One twig at a time. Their nests are famously minimal. They like it that way.

variants.title: A pigeon is flying one perfect twig home
variants.body: Somewhere on a ledge above {street} there's a nest in progress. City pigeons build any time of year, one twig at a time, a few floors above everyone's heads.

variants.title: The pigeons are wearing their puffy coats
variants.body: Feathers fluffed into a down jacket, pressed together where the sun hits the building.

variants.title: Pigeon huddle in progress
variants.body: Shoulder to shoulder on the sunny side of the ledge. Warmth shared is warmth doubled.

variants.title: The pigeons are huddled on the sunny side of {landmark}
variants.body: Shoulder to shoulder, fluffed up like little gray pillows, waiting for the sun to warm their ledge. They share the warmth, so nobody gets too cold.

variants.title: The pigeons are back on the ledge
variants.body: Pairs settle in side by side. Same ledge, same partner, every single night.

variants.title: Pigeon bedtime is starting
variants.body: One by one they flap up to the ledge {place} and shuffle in next to their favorite pigeon.

variants.title: The pigeons are coming home to their ledge
variants.body: As the light goes, pairs flap up above {street} and settle in side by side. Same ledge, same partner, every night, like they've been doing for years.

variants.title: The pigeons are asleep on the ledge
variants.body: Heads tucked into their back feathers, pressed together in pairs, a few floors above the sidewalk {place}.

variants.title: A pigeon is dozing on one foot
variants.body: Feathers fluffed, head tucked. City noise doesn't bother them one bit.

variants.title: The pigeons are asleep above {street}
variants.body: Heads tucked into their back feathers, pressed together in pairs on the ledges. Below them, the neighborhood keeps humming. They don't mind one bit.

variants.title: The sparrow gang is up and talking
variants.body: The hedge {place} is chattering away. That racket is how they keep track of who's where. Also gossip, probably.

variants.title: Good morning from the hedge
variants.body: Cheep, cheep, CHEEP. The sparrows have opinions about the day already.

variants.title: The sparrow gang is waking up the block
variants.body: The hedges along {street} are suddenly full of chatter. It's how they check in every morning: who's here, who found food, who's being dramatic.

variants.title: The sparrows are taking a dust bath
variants.body: They wriggle into a dry patch of dirt and flick it through their feathers. It's dry shampoo, sparrow style.

variants.title: Sparrow spa day at the curb
variants.body: Wiggle, flap, fluff, repeat. Dust scrubs away oil and tiny bugs. They come out cleaner, somehow.

variants.title: The sparrows are having a dust bath near {green}
variants.body: They've found a dry patch of dirt and they're wriggling in it like it's a spa. A good dust bath keeps their feathers clean. Also, it looks extremely fun.

variants.title: Sparrow kids are begging very dramatically
variants.body: Fluffy youngsters chase their parents, wings fluttering, beaks wide open. The parents mostly give in.

variants.title: A baby sparrow is following a grown-up everywhere
variants.body: Flutter, flutter, CHEEP. The grown-up finds a bug, the baby finds a way to be standing right there.

variants.title: Baby sparrows are begging all over {street}
variants.body: Fluffy youngsters chase their parents from curb to hedge, wings fluttering, mouths wide open. The grown-ups look tired. They keep feeding them anyway.

variants.title: A sparrow is stuffing grass into a gap
variants.body: A sign, a traffic light, a hole in old brick: anywhere will do for a messy, cozy nest. Interior design: maximal.

variants.title: Sparrow construction season is open
variants.body: Bits of grass, feathers and string go into every nook {place}. The result is lumpy and perfect.

variants.title: A sparrow is moving into a gap near {landmark}
variants.body: Grass, feathers, a bit of string: they're stuffing it all into a crack in the old brick. It won't win any design awards. It will be very cozy.

variants.title: The hedge is having its evening meeting
variants.body: Before bed, the whole gang gathers in the bushes and talks over the day. Loudly. Everyone has a point.

variants.title: The sparrows are arguing about bedtime
variants.body: Lots of chirping, lots of shuffling, then suddenly, quiet. They've settled it.

variants.title: The hedge on {street} is having its evening meeting
variants.body: Every sparrow on the block is in there, chattering about the day before bed. Then, all at once, it goes quiet. Meeting adjourned.

variants.title: The sparrows are tiny fluffballs today
variants.body: Puffed up round, shoulder to shoulder, deep in the hedge and out of the wind.

variants.title: Sparrow sleepover in the hedge
variants.body: It's cold, so everyone's packed in close. Small birds, big huddle.

variants.title: The sparrows are huddled deep in the hedge
variants.body: Puffed into round little balls, packed shoulder to shoulder out of the wind along {street}. Small birds, big huddle, warm enough.

variants.title: The sparrow gang is asleep in the hedge
variants.body: Deep inside the bushes, all puffed up together. The chatter starts again at first light. Count on it.

variants.title: Lights out in the hedge
variants.body: For a few hours, the loudest bushes {place} are completely quiet.

variants.title: Lights out in the sparrow hedge
variants.body: Deep in the bushes along {street}, the whole gang is asleep, feathers fluffed. The loudest hedge in the neighborhood is finally, completely quiet.

variants.title: A squirrel is hiding an acorn
variants.body: Dig, drop, pat-pat-pat, then a very suspicious look around. You saw nothing.

variants.title: Squirrels are accidentally planting next year's trees
variants.body: Every planter {place} is a pantry right now. The acorns they forget will sprout in spring. Oops, a forest.

variants.title: A squirrel is pretending to bury something
variants.body: If they think someone's watching, they'll fake it: dig, pat, nothing there. The real snack goes somewhere secret.

variants.title: A squirrel is planting an acorn in {green}
variants.body: Dig, drop, pat-pat-pat, then a quick look around to see who's watching. They'll find a lot of these again by memory. The ones they forget might be oak trees someday.

variants.title: The squirrels are up and digging
variants.body: Morning is rush hour. They're checking old hiding spots and sniffing out breakfast {place}.

variants.title: A squirrel is speed-running the lawn
variants.body: Dash, stop, sniff, dig, dash. They have a lot of places to check before lunch.

variants.title: The squirrels are making their morning rounds
variants.body: Up and down the trees on {street}, checking old hiding spots, sniffing for breakfast. Morning is their busiest time, and they have a lot of spots to check.

variants.title: Two squirrels are chasing each other around the tree
variants.body: Wild spirals up and down the trunk. It's courting season, and nobody is being subtle about it.

variants.title: Squirrel loop-de-loops on the tree trunk
variants.body: Round and round and round. In winter, these chases are mostly about romance. Very dizzy romance.

variants.title: Two squirrels are chasing circles around a tree
variants.body: Up, down and around the trunk near {green}, so fast it's dizzying. It's winter courting season, and nobody's being subtle about it.

variants.title: A squirrel is splooting
variants.body: Flat on a cool branch, belly down, legs out like a little rug. That's how a squirrel beats the heat.

variants.title: Squirrel pancake on the branch
variants.body: Too hot to scamper. They've spread out flat in the shade and they are not getting up.

variants.title: A squirrel is lying flat as a pancake
variants.body: Stretched belly-down on a cool branch over {street}, legs out, done with the heat. It's called splooting, and it's the most relatable thing in nature.

variants.title: A squirrel mom is heading home to the drey
variants.body: Babies are tucked up in that ball of leaves. She checks on them between snack runs.

variants.title: Busy mom, coming through
variants.body: Up the trunk to the leafy nest, quick check on the kits, and back down for more snacks.

variants.title: A squirrel mom is checking on her babies
variants.body: Up the trunk to a ball of leaves high above {green}. Her kits are tucked inside. She'll peek in, then head back out for more snacks.

variants.title: A squirrel is heading up for the night
variants.body: Up the trunk to the drey, tail flicking. Bedtime comes early for squirrels.

variants.title: Last snack, then bed
variants.body: One final nibble, then straight up the tree. Squirrels keep very responsible hours.

variants.title: A squirrel is heading up for the night
variants.body: One last snack near {green}, then straight up the tree to the leafy drey. Squirrels keep sensible hours. Lights out early.

variants.title: A squirrel is curled up in the drey
variants.body: Wrapped in their own tail like a blanket, high in a ball of leaves. On cold nights, sometimes two share.

variants.title: Squirrel, fast asleep in a leaf ball
variants.body: That messy clump of leaves up in the tree {place}? There's a very cozy squirrel inside.

variants.title: A squirrel is fast asleep in the drey
variants.body: High in a tree near {green}, curled inside a ball of leaves, tail wrapped around like a blanket. On cold nights, sometimes two squirrels share.

variants.title: The starlings are lining up on the wire
variants.body: Dozens of them, chattering, before heading off together to a shared roost for the night.

variants.title: A starling is doing impressions
variants.body: Listen: a whistle, a click, maybe a car alarm. Starlings borrow sounds from the street {place} and remix them into songs.

variants.title: Starling group chat, live on the wire
variants.body: So much chatter. Then, all at once, everybody takes off. Meeting adjourned.

variants.title: The starlings are gathering on the wires over {street}
variants.body: Dozens of them, chattering and swapping places, before they all take off together toward their night roost. Listen closely: some of those sounds are borrowed from the neighborhood.

variants.title: Starlings are poking holes in the lawn
variants.body: They stab their beaks into the grass and open them wide to pry up grubs. A clever little trick.

variants.title: The starlings are lawn-aerating for free
variants.body: Poke, open, snack. They march across the grass like a tiny, very shiny work crew.

variants.title: The starlings are working the grass at {green}
variants.body: They push their beaks into the lawn and pop them open to pry up grubs. It's a clever little trick, and they march across the grass like a shiny work crew.

variants.title: A starling is putting on a rooftop concert
variants.body: All dressed up in glossy purple and green, wings flicking, singing every sound they know.

variants.title: A starling is singing from a chimney
variants.body: Whistles, clicks, a borrowed car alarm. Spring starlings are very committed performers.

variants.title: A starling is singing from a chimney above {street}
variants.body: Glossy purple and green, wings flicking, mixing whistles and clicks and maybe a car alarm into one long spring song. They put their whole heart into it.

variants.title: Young starlings are following their parents around
variants.body: Plain brown and very loud, they trail the grown-ups across the grass begging for bugs.

variants.title: Starling teens are being extremely loud
variants.body: They look nothing like the shiny grown-ups yet, but the volume is already perfect.

variants.title: Young starlings are following their parents across {green}
variants.body: Plain brown and very loud, they trail the shiny grown-ups across the grass, begging for bugs. They'll get their spots soon enough.

variants.title: The starlings are wearing their stars
variants.body: Their winter feathers are covered in white speckles. Catch one in the sun and they sparkle.

variants.title: Starling, polka dots edition
variants.body: In winter they're dark and spotted all over, like a little starry sky with legs.

variants.title: The starlings are sparkling in the winter sun
variants.body: Perched on a wire over {street}, covered in tiny white speckles. When the light hits just right, they look like little starry skies.

variants.title: A mourning dove is cooing
variants.body: That soft, slow hoo-OO-oo-oo isn't sad at all. It's a love song from a wire {place}.

variants.title: A mourning dove is going hoo-OO-oo-oo
variants.body: The mourning dove sounds a bit gloomy, but that's actually flirting.

variants.title: A mourning dove is cooing softly on {street}
variants.body: Hoo-OO-oo-oo, from a wire somewhere above. It sounds a little sad, but it's a love song, and someone nearby is probably listening.

variants.title: Two doves are sitting very close
variants.body: Side by side on the wire, preening each other. Mourning doves usually come in pairs. Adorable, honestly.

variants.title: A dove couple is sharing the wire
variants.body: A little nudge, a little preen. They're doing their best impression of a valentine.

variants.title: Two mourning doves are sitting close together
variants.body: Side by side on a wire near {green}, gently preening each other. Doves usually come in pairs, and these two look perfectly content.

variants.title: A dove is building the world's simplest nest
variants.body: A few twigs on a fire escape. Somehow, it's enough. Minimalism wins again.

variants.title: Mourning dove, nest-building on a budget
variants.body: Twig, twig, done. Their nests are so thin you can sometimes see the eggs from below.

variants.title: A dove is building a tiny nest near {landmark}
variants.body: A few twigs balanced on a fire escape or a ledge. It doesn't look like much, but it's enough, and in a couple of weeks there might be chicks.

variants.title: Mourning doves are picking at seeds
variants.body: A small group walks the ground, bobbing their heads. When they take off, listen for the whistle of their wings.

variants.title: Head-bob parade on the ground
variants.body: The doves are strolling and snacking. If you startle them, their wings squeak like a toy.

variants.title: Mourning doves are strolling through {green}
variants.body: A little group walks the ground, bobbing their heads and picking up seeds. If something startles them, listen for the soft whistle of their wings.

variants.title: The doves are soaking up the last sun
variants.body: Puffed up on the wire, facing the sunset, catching every bit of warmth before night.

variants.title: Dove, fluffed up to maximum
variants.body: Round as a dinner roll, eyes half closed, enjoying the last warm light {place}.

variants.title: The doves are catching the last warm light
variants.body: Puffed up round on a wire over {street}, facing the sunset, soaking in every bit of warmth before the night comes.

variants.title: A robin is kicking off the dawn chorus
variants.body: Before the sun is up, one robin sings, then another. Listen for a cheery, rolling song {place}.

variants.title: The robins are up before everyone
variants.body: It's still mostly dark, and they're already singing like it's the best morning ever.

variants.title: A robin is singing the neighborhood awake
variants.body: It's barely light, and a robin near {green} is already singing. Then another answers from down {street}. The dawn chorus has begun.

variants.title: A robin is hunting worms
variants.body: Run, stop, tilt the head, pounce. That tilt isn't listening: they're looking at the ground with one eye.

variants.title: Robin vs. worm, round one
variants.body: A tug, a stretch, a tug. The robin usually wins. The worm puts up a good fight.

variants.title: A robin is hunting worms in {green}
variants.body: Run, stop, tilt, pounce. That head tilt isn't listening: robins look at the ground with one eye, searching for the tiniest wiggle.

variants.title: A robin fledgling is figuring things out
variants.body: Spotty chest, stubby tail, lots of hopping. A parent is nearby with a worm. No rescue needed.

variants.title: Baby robin, hopping around like a wind-up toy
variants.body: They can't fly well yet, but mom and dad are watching. Give them space and they'll be fine.

variants.title: A baby robin is hopping around {green}
variants.body: Spotty chest, stubby tail, not quite flying yet. A parent is close by with a worm. This little one is right where they're supposed to be.

variants.title: The robins are raiding the berry bushes
variants.body: Worms are getting scarce, so they've switched to fruit. A group can clear a tree in an afternoon.

variants.title: Robin berry buffet is open
variants.body: Gulp, gulp, gulp. In fall and winter, robins go full fruit mode.

variants.title: The robins are feasting on berries near {green}
variants.body: Worms are getting scarce, so they've switched to fruit. A whole flock can clear a berry tree in an afternoon, gulping happily the whole time.

variants.title: A robin is singing the day out
variants.body: First to sing in the morning and among the last at night. Long shift. Great attitude.

variants.title: One more song from the robin
variants.body: As the light fades {place}, a robin is still going, cheerful as ever.

variants.title: A robin is singing the day out
variants.body: As the light fades over {street}, one robin is still going, cheerful as ever. First voice in the morning, one of the last at night.

variants.title: A quiet flock of robins is passing through
variants.body: Plenty of robins stay all winter. They stop singing and travel in groups, looking for berries.

variants.title: Surprise, the robins never left
variants.body: In winter they're quieter and hang out in flocks, so you might not notice them. They're here.

variants.title: A quiet flock of robins is passing through {green}
variants.body: Plenty of robins stay all winter. They stop singing and travel together, looking for berries, so you might not notice them. They're still your neighbors.

variants.title: The robins are at a big sleepover
variants.body: Dads and young robins often sleep together in one big group roost, then scatter at dawn.

variants.title: Robins, roosting in the trees
variants.body: Dozens of them tucked into the branches, getting rested for tomorrow's very early concert.

variants.title: The robins are at their big sleepover
variants.body: Dozens tucked into the trees near {green}, sleeping together in one group roost. At dawn, they'll scatter back to their own patches.

variants.title: A gull is riding the wind
variants.body: Wings barely moving, drifting over the rooftops {place} like it's no effort at all. It mostly isn't.

variants.title: A gull is just hanging in the air
variants.body: No flapping, no hurry. They found the perfect breeze and they're keeping it.

variants.title: A gull is gliding over {water}
variants.body: Wings out, barely moving, riding the breeze off the water like it costs nothing. Every so often they tilt, just a little, and the whole sky turns with them.

variants.title: A gull is cracking a clam the clever way
variants.body: Up, up, then drop it on the rocks. If it doesn't break, they'll try again. And again. Persistence!

variants.title: Gull vs. clam
variants.body: The gull has a plan: fly high, let go, check the result. Repeat until lunch is served.

variants.title: A gull is cracking a clam on the rocks by {water}
variants.body: Up high, then drop. Check it. Not yet? Up again. It's a clever trick, and they'll keep at it until lunch is served.

variants.title: A gull has claimed a piling
variants.body: Watching the water {place}, waiting to see what the morning tide brings in. That piling is taken.

variants.title: Gull, on morning lookout
variants.body: Standing very tall on a post, judging the harbor. Breakfast could show up any minute.

variants.title: A gull is keeping watch from a post on {water}
variants.body: Standing tall, feathers ruffling, watching the morning water for whatever the tide brings in. That post is theirs, and everyone knows it.

variants.title: The gulls are heading out to the water for the night
variants.body: They sleep floating together on the harbor, safe from anything on land.

variants.title: Gull commute, outbound
variants.body: As the sun goes down, the gulls fly out over the water to their floating bedroom.

variants.title: The gulls are flying out to {water} for the night
variants.body: As the sky turns pink, they head out over the water to sleep floating together, far from anything on land.

variants.title: A gull is guarding a rooftop nest
variants.body: Gulls nest on flat roofs around the city. Get too close and you'll hear about it. Loudly.

variants.title: Gull parent on roof duty
variants.body: Somewhere up there is a nest. The gull standing guard takes the job very seriously.

variants.title: A gull is guarding a nest on a rooftop near {street}
variants.body: Up on a flat roof, a gull parent stands watch over a nest. Get too close and you'll hear about it. Gulls take parenting very seriously.

variants.title: A young gull is whining for lunch
variants.body: Mottled brown and as big as the grown-ups, still begging. The red spot on a parent's beak is the doorbell.

variants.title: Gull teenager, still asking parents for food
variants.body: Full-size, fully capable, extremely whiny. They'll get there.

variants.title: A young gull is whining for lunch by {water}
variants.body: Mottled brown, already as big as the grown-ups, and still begging. The red spot on a parent's beak is the doorbell, and this kid keeps ringing it.

variants.title: Shh, the gulls are finally asleep
variants.body: All tucked in together on the harbor, bobbing like bath toys. For once, nobody is yelling.

variants.title: The gulls are asleep on the water
variants.body: Floating out on the harbor, rising and falling with the waves, safe from anything on land.

variants.title: The gulls are asleep out on {water}
variants.body: Floating together, tucked in, bobbing like bath toys on the night water. For once, the loudest birds in the neighborhood are completely quiet.

variants.title: A monarch is drinking from the flowers
variants.body: Wings opening and closing slowly in the sun. Every sip is fuel for a very big trip.

variants.title: Monarch at the snack bar
variants.body: Flower to flower, sip, sip. That orange is a warning to birds: they taste terrible.

variants.title: A monarch is drinking from the flowers in {green}
variants.body: Wings opening and closing slowly in the sun, moving bloom to bloom. Every sip is fuel for a long trip, and this one is taking it seriously.

variants.title: A monarch is flying to Mexico
variants.body: This butterfly is headed to the mountains of Mexico, a place they've never been. Today's stop: a snack break {place}. No map needed.

variants.title: Tiny traveler, passing through
variants.body: A monarch is drifting south over the rooftops. Thousands of miles to go, one flap at a time.

variants.title: A monarch is passing through {green} on the way to Mexico
variants.body: This butterfly has never been to the mountains of Mexico, but they know the way. Today's stop: a quick rest and a snack, right here.

variants.title: A monarch is laying eggs on milkweed
variants.body: One tiny egg per leaf. Milkweed is the only plant their caterpillars can eat. Picky, but loyal.

variants.title: Monarch mom, very particular about milkweed
variants.body: She tastes the leaves with her feet before leaving an egg. Only the best for the kids.

variants.title: A monarch is leaving eggs on milkweed near {green}
variants.body: She tastes each leaf with her feet before leaving one tiny egg. Milkweed is the only plant her caterpillars can eat, so she's very particular.

variants.title: The monarchs are settling in for the night
variants.body: Travelers rest together on branches, wings folded, before tomorrow's leg of the trip.

variants.title: Monarch hotel, now open
variants.body: A few butterflies are bunking on the same branch {place}. Big day of flying tomorrow.

variants.title: Monarchs are resting together near {green}
variants.body: A few travelers have folded their wings on the same branch for the night. Tomorrow they'll keep flying south. Tonight, they rest.

variants.title: A red-tailed hawk is sitting very, very still
variants.body: Up on a ledge {place}, watching the ground below. They can wait an hour for one good chance.

variants.title: Hawk on a light pole, doing nothing on purpose
variants.body: It looks like a nap. It is not a nap. They're watching everything.

variants.title: A red-tailed hawk is watching over {street}
variants.body: Up on {landmark}, perfectly still, eyes on the ground below. They can wait a whole hour for one good chance. Patience is their superpower.

variants.title: A hawk is circling overhead
variants.body: Wide, lazy loops on rising warm air. Look for the rusty red tail when they bank.

variants.title: Free elevator ride for the hawk
variants.body: They ride warm air up and up without flapping. Effortless, and a little show-offy.

variants.title: A hawk is circling high above {green}
variants.body: Wide, slow loops on rising warm air, hardly a single flap. When they bank, look for the rusty red tail glowing in the sun.

variants.title: Two red-tails are on a sky date
variants.body: Soaring together in big circles. Sometimes one dives and they touch talons in the air. Very dramatic.

variants.title: Red-tailed hawk romance, overhead
variants.body: Matching loops, a swoop, a near miss on purpose. Winter is courting season.

variants.title: Two red-tailed hawks are dancing in the sky
variants.body: Soaring together above {green} in matching circles. Sometimes one dives toward the other and they touch talons midair. Winter is their season for romance.

variants.title: A red-tail is sitting on eggs
variants.body: In a big stick nest on a building or a tall tree. Their partner brings dinner. Good partner.

variants.title: Hawk, on nest duty
variants.body: Hunkered down on a giant pile of sticks, keeping the eggs warm while the city goes by.

variants.title: A red-tail is keeping eggs warm near {landmark}
variants.body: In a big nest of sticks on a ledge or a tall tree, a hawk sits very still. Their partner brings dinner. Good partner.

variants.title: A young hawk is screaming for dinner
variants.body: That long wheeze is a fledgling asking the parents to hurry up while they learn to hunt.

variants.title: Hawk teen, very loud, very hungry
variants.body: They can fly now, but hunting is hard. So they yell. A lot.

variants.title: A young hawk is calling for dinner over {green}
variants.body: That long, wheezy scream is a fledgling asking the parents to hurry up. They can fly now. Hunting is still a work in progress.

variants.title: A hawk is tucking in for the night
variants.body: Perched close to a tree trunk, out of the wind, done for the day.

variants.title: Hawk, off the clock
variants.body: Shift's over. Feathers fluffed, tucked against the trunk, eyes closing.

variants.title: A hawk is settling in for the night
variants.body: Perched close against a tree trunk near {green}, out of the wind, feathers fluffed. Shift's over. Tomorrow, the watch begins again.

variants.title: A blue jay is stuffing acorns in their throat
variants.body: They can carry several at once in a stretchy throat pouch. The ones they forget grow into oaks {place}.

variants.title: Blue jay, burying treasure
variants.body: Acorn here, acorn there. Jays plant more oak trees than most people ever will.

variants.title: A blue jay is planting oaks around {green}
variants.body: They carry acorns in a stretchy pouch in their throat and bury them all over. The ones they forget sprout, so this jay is quietly growing a forest.

variants.title: A blue jay is pretending to be a hawk
variants.body: That hawk scream might be a jay. Maybe it clears everyone off the good branch. Maybe it's just fun.

variants.title: That hawk scream is really a blue jay
variants.body: Nope. That's a blue jay doing their best hawk impression. They're very good at it.

variants.title: A blue jay is doing their best hawk impression
variants.body: That scream from the trees near {green}? Probably a jay. They copy hawks so well it can clear the whole branch. Maybe that's the point. Maybe it's just fun.

variants.title: A blue jay is announcing the morning
variants.body: JAY! JAY! Bright blue against bare branches, and very loud about it.

variants.title: A blue jay is shouting good morning
variants.body: No alarm clock needed {place}. The jays have it covered.

variants.title: A blue jay is announcing the morning
variants.body: JAY! JAY! from a bare branch over {street}. Bright blue, very loud, absolutely sure everyone should be awake by now.

variants.title: A blue jay is being suspiciously quiet
variants.body: Near their nest, the loudest bird on the block slips in and out without a sound.

variants.title: Blue jay in stealth mode
variants.body: Usually the loudest bird around. Right now, sneaky as a spy. There's a nest nearby.

variants.title: A blue jay is being suspiciously quiet
variants.body: Usually the loudest bird around {green}. Right now, slipping silently through the leaves. That means there's a nest nearby, and they're keeping it secret.

variants.title: A blue jay family is on a field trip
variants.body: The youngsters follow the grown-ups through the trees and copy everything they do.

variants.title: Young blue jays are learning the ropes
variants.body: Watch a grown-up, try it, mess it up, try again. Very relatable.

variants.title: A blue jay family is on a field trip through {green}
variants.body: The youngsters follow the grown-ups from tree to tree, copying everything they do. Watch, try, mess up, try again.

variants.title: Juncos are hopping under the hedge
variants.body: Little gray birds with snowy bellies, scratching for seeds. When they fly, their tails flash white.

variants.title: Tiny snowbirds, hop-hop-hopping
variants.body: Juncos never walk. They hop. Everywhere. Under every bush {place}.

variants.title: Juncos are hopping under the hedges on {street}
variants.body: Little gray birds with snowy bellies, scratching through the leaves for seeds. They don't walk, they hop. And when they fly, their tails flash white.

variants.title: The first juncos just landed
variants.body: They flew down from Canada overnight and touched down {place}. They'll stay till spring.

variants.title: The snowbirds are back
variants.body: Juncos tend to show up right as it gets chilly. Welcome back, little gray friends.

variants.title: The juncos just arrived from Canada
variants.body: They flew all night and landed near {green} this morning. They'll spend the whole winter here, hopping under the hedges. Welcome back, snowbirds.

variants.title: A junco is trilling before the trip north
variants.body: A quick, bright trill from a branch. In a few weeks they'll be gone till fall.

variants.title: Junco, warming up for the road
variants.body: A little trill, a lot of snacking. Canada is a long way to fly.

variants.title: A junco is trilling before the trip north
variants.body: A quick, bright song from a branch near {green}. In a few weeks they'll head back to Canada. Until then, lots of snacks and practice songs.

variants.title: The juncos are tucking into the hedge for the night
variants.body: A small flock huddles low in the bushes, out of the wind.

variants.title: Junco bedtime, low and cozy
variants.body: They pick the thickest part of the hedge and scoot in close together.

variants.title: The juncos are tucking into the hedge for the night
variants.body: A little flock scoots low into the thickest part of the bushes along {street}, out of the wind, close together.

variants.title: The juncos are asleep low in the hedge
variants.body: Tucked close to the ground, out of the wind, saving every bit of warmth for tomorrow.

variants.title: Little gray puffballs, fast asleep
variants.body: Somewhere under a hedge {place}, a few juncos are snoozing close together.

variants.title: The juncos are asleep under the hedge
variants.body: Somewhere along {street}, a few little gray puffballs are snoozing close to the ground, saving their warmth for tomorrow.

variants.title: The crows are commuting home
variants.body: Long lines of them cross the sky at dusk, all heading to the same few roosts to sleep together.

variants.title: Crow rush hour, overhead
variants.body: Caw, caw, caw. Everyone's heading to the big sleepover at once.

variants.title: The crows are commuting home over {street}
variants.body: Long, loose lines of them, cawing to each other, all headed to the same big roost to sleep together. It's crow rush hour.

variants.title: The crows are heading to work
variants.body: Thousands slept together last night. Now each family heads back to their own patch, maybe {place}.

variants.title: Crow families are fanning out for the day
variants.body: One big roost, many little neighborhoods. Everybody knows their route.

variants.title: The crows are heading back to their neighborhoods
variants.body: After a night in the big roost, each family flies home to their own patch. One of those families lives around {green}. They know every rooftop.

variants.title: A crow is keeping an eye on things
variants.body: Crows remember faces. Be friendly and you might get a nod back. They're excellent judges of character.

variants.title: The neighborhood watch is on duty
variants.body: A crow on the roof edge is noting who's who {place}. They really do remember people.

variants.title: A crow is keeping an eye on {street}
variants.body: Perched on {landmark}, watching who comes and goes. Crows remember faces for years. Be kind, and you might get a nod back someday.

variants.title: Crow big siblings are on babysitting duty
variants.body: Last year's kids help out. Big sisters and brothers bring food to the nest.

variants.title: A crow family is feeding the new chicks
variants.body: It takes a village. Or at least a few older siblings with snacks.

variants.title: A crow family is raising the new chicks together
variants.body: In a tall tree near {green}, last year's kids are helping out, bringing food to their new little siblings. It takes a family.

variants.title: Young crows are begging loudly
variants.body: Fluffy, noisy and following the parents everywhere. Patience is not a crow-kid skill.

variants.title: Crow kid, very sure they're starving
variants.body: They aren't. But they'd like everyone {place} to know they could eat.

variants.title: Young crows are begging loudly near {green}
variants.body: Fluffy, noisy and following their parents everywhere, absolutely convinced they're starving. They aren't. Patience is not a crow-kid skill.

variants.title: The crows are at a giant sleepover
variants.body: Hundreds, sometimes thousands, packed into the same stand of trees. There's safety in numbers.

variants.title: Crow roost, lights out
variants.body: A whole city of crows, sleeping shoulder to shoulder in the trees.

variants.title: The crows are sleeping together tonight
variants.body: Hundreds of crows, maybe thousands, packed into one stand of trees. Somewhere in there is the family from around {green}. Safety in numbers.

variants.title: A White-throated Sparrow is whistling
variants.body: Oh sweet Canada, Canada, Canada. A thin, clear song from the bushes {place}.

variants.title: Someone in the bushes is singing about Canada
variants.body: That's a White-throated Sparrow. Very homesick song, very pretty.

variants.title: A White-throated Sparrow is singing about Canada
variants.body: Oh sweet Canada, Canada, Canada, a thin, clear whistle from the bushes near {green}. It's one of the loveliest sounds of the season.

variants.title: White-throated Sparrows are doing the leaf kick
variants.body: Both feet at once, hop-kick backward. They're finding bugs and seeds under the leaves.

variants.title: The White-throated Sparrows are doing their hop-kick dance
variants.body: The White-throated Sparrows have a whole dance for finding snacks in the leaf litter.

variants.title: White-throated Sparrows are doing the leaf kick
variants.body: Both feet at once, hop-kick backward, in the leaf litter near {green}. They're uncovering seeds and bugs, one little kick at a time.

variants.title: The White-throated Sparrows are back
variants.body: They flew in from Canadian forests and will spend the winter in the bushes here.

variants.title: New neighbors in the bushes
variants.body: White-throated Sparrows just moved in for the season. Listen for their whistle.

variants.title: The White-throated Sparrows are back for the winter
variants.body: They flew down from the forests of Canada and moved into the bushes around {green}. Listen for their whistle all season long.

variants.title: White-throated Sparrows are fueling up
variants.body: In a few weeks they'll head north. Right now it's all snacks and practice songs.

variants.title: Snack break before the big trip
variants.body: The White-throated Sparrows are eating everything they can find. Canada's far.

variants.title: White-throated Sparrows are fueling up for the trip north
variants.body: Snacking under the bushes near {green}, and practicing their song. In a few weeks they'll be gone till fall.

variants.title: Chimney swifts are zipping overhead
variants.body: Tiny cigar-shaped birds, twittering, catching bugs on the wing. They hardly ever land.

variants.title: Flying cigars, twittering
variants.body: Those little zoomy birds are chimney swifts. They eat, drink and bathe without landing.

variants.title: Chimney swifts are zipping over {street}
variants.body: Tiny cigar-shaped birds, twittering, swooping, catching bugs on the wing. They eat, drink and even bathe without landing.

variants.title: The swifts are pouring into a chimney
variants.body: As the light goes, they circle and swirl down into an old chimney {place} to sleep, clinging to the inside wall.

variants.title: Swift tornado, right on schedule
variants.body: Round and round, then whoosh, they all drop into the chimney for the night.

variants.title: The swifts are pouring into an old chimney
variants.body: At dusk they swirl together above {street}, round and round, then funnel down into a chimney all at once, to sleep clinging to the inside wall.

variants.title: The chimney swifts are back
variants.body: Fresh in from South America. Listen for high twittering over the rooftops.

variants.title: Twitter, twitter, the swifts have landed
variants.body: Well, not landed. They barely ever land. But they're back!

variants.title: The chimney swifts are back over {street}
variants.body: Fresh in from South America after a very long trip. Listen for their high twittering over the rooftops: summer is on its way.

variants.title: A goose family is out for a walk
variants.body: Mom in front, dad at the back, and a line of fuzzy yellow goslings in between. Nobody is allowed to cut in.

variants.title: The goslings are learning to graze
variants.body: Tiny beaks, very serious faces, one blade of grass at a time. A parent stands guard with a stare that says keep walking.

variants.title: A goose family is parading toward {water}
variants.body: Two grown-ups and a wobbly line of goslings, crossing the grass near {green} like they own it. In a way, they do.

variants.title: The geese are grounded for a few weeks
variants.body: Every summer they drop their flight feathers and grow new ones. Until then, it's floating, grazing and laying low.

variants.title: Geese are taking a summer break from flying
variants.body: No feathers, no flights. They stick close to the water, where a quick paddle away keeps them safe.

variants.title: The geese are spending the summer by {water}
variants.body: While their new flight feathers grow in, they stay close to the water's edge, grazing and floating and keeping a low profile.

variants.title: A V of geese is honking overhead
variants.body: They take turns at the front, where the flying is hardest. The honking is how they keep the line together.

variants.title: Geese are flying in formation
variants.body: That big wobbly V is a flock on the move, chatting the whole way. Listen before you look.

variants.title: A honking V is passing over {green}
variants.body: High and loud, a flock is crossing the sky above the neighborhood, taking turns at the front and talking the whole way.

variants.title: A goose is standing on one foot
variants.body: The other foot is tucked up in their warm belly feathers. They'll switch feet when this one gets cold.

variants.title: Geese are lined up along the frozen edge
variants.body: Feathers fluffed, heads tucked, one foot up. Winter strategy: stay together, stay still, stay warm.

variants.title: The geese are wintering by {water}
variants.body: A flock is resting at the edge of the water, heads tucked and one foot up, waiting out the cold together.

variants.title: A mallard mom has a line of ducklings
variants.body: Paddle, paddle, peep. They follow her everywhere, and she keeps a very close count.

variants.title: Ducklings are speed-paddling to keep up
variants.body: Tiny feet going like crazy, mom gliding along like it's nothing. Every so often one zooms off and zooms right back.

variants.title: A mallard mom is leading her ducklings around {water}
variants.body: Single file, a little fluffy parade, past the reeds and along the edge. She's showing them every good snack spot.

variants.title: A mallard is doing a perfect handstand
variants.body: Head underwater, tail straight up, feet paddling the air. It's how they reach the good plants at the bottom.

variants.title: Bottoms up at the pond
variants.body: A row of duck tails pointing at the sky. Lunch is down there somewhere.

variants.title: The mallards are dabbling at {water}
variants.body: Tip forward, tail up, nibble, pop back up. They're snacking on the water plants along the edge, very pleased with themselves.

variants.title: Two mallards are paddling side by side
variants.body: Mallards pair up in fall and winter. He's in his shiny green head; she's in her cozy brown.

variants.title: The mallard with the green head is showing off
variants.body: Head bob, tail flick, a little whistle. Courting season on the pond has begun.

variants.title: Mallard couples are floating on {water}
variants.body: Two by two, paddling slowly together. They'll stay paired through the winter.

variants.title: The mallards are asleep at the water's edge
variants.body: Heads tucked over their backs, bills under a wing, tucked in among the reeds.

variants.title: Mallards are napping on the water
variants.body: Some sleep floating, with one eye open just in case. Very relaxing, very alert.

variants.title: The ducks are sleeping by {water}
variants.body: Tucked into the reeds, heads turned back, bills under their wings. A few soft quacks now and then.

variants.title: The brant just flew in from the Arctic
variants.body: Thousands of miles, and now they're here for the winter. Listen for their low, rolling cronk.

variants.title: Small dark geese are back on the shore
variants.body: Brant are here! They spend the summer on the Arctic tundra and the winter right here.

variants.title: The brant have landed by {water}
variants.body: Fresh in from the Arctic, a flock is grazing along the shore. They'll stay till spring.

variants.title: A flock of brant is grazing the lawn
variants.body: Little dark geese with white necklaces, chatting away and nibbling grass by the water.

variants.title: The brant are munching sea lettuce
variants.body: Their favorite winter snack grows right along the rocks at low tide. Crunchy, salty, perfect.

variants.title: Brant are grazing near {green}
variants.body: A chatty flock is working their way across the grass by the water, one nibble at a time, little white necklaces bobbing.

variants.title: The brant are fueling up for the Arctic
variants.body: Eating as much as they can. In May they'll fly thousands of miles north.

variants.title: Brant are getting restless
variants.body: More chatter, more flying around. Any day now they'll head for the Arctic.

variants.title: The brant are saying goodbye to {water}
variants.body: A noisy flock is bobbing near the shore, getting ready for the long flight back to the Arctic.

variants.title: A cormorant is drying their wings
variants.body: Standing on a post, wings held wide like a little cape. Their feathers soak up water, so they air-dry after every swim.

variants.title: A cormorant is striking a pose
variants.body: Wings out, chin up, very dramatic. It's not showing off. It's laundry day.

variants.title: A cormorant is drying off on a post in {water}
variants.body: Wings spread wide in the sun, perfectly still, after a long swim chasing fish.

variants.title: A cormorant just disappeared underwater
variants.body: They swim after fish using their feet, sometimes for half a minute. Watch where they pop back up.

variants.title: Cormorant on a fishing trip
variants.body: Dive, chase, gulp. They swallow fish headfirst, right at the surface.

variants.title: A cormorant is fishing in {water}
variants.body: Bob, dive, gone. Somewhere under the surface, a cormorant is chasing lunch.

variants.title: A line of cormorants is flying south
variants.body: Low over the water in a long, loose line. Winter plans: somewhere warmer.

variants.title: Cormorants are heading out
variants.body: A string of dark birds skims over the water, wing beats steady, on their way south.

variants.title: Cormorants are flying low over {water}
variants.body: A long line of dark birds, heading south for the winter.

variants.title: Ring-billed gulls have taken over the field
variants.body: Dozens of them, standing around facing into the wind. Very organized, for gulls.

variants.title: A ring-billed gull is checking the picnic area
variants.body: Not begging. Just... supervising. Very closely.

variants.title: Ring-billed gulls are lounging near {green}
variants.body: A whole crowd of neat gray-and-white gulls, all facing the same way into the breeze, chatting.

variants.title: A ring-billed gull is patrolling the shore
variants.body: Walking the waterline, checking what the tide brought in. Every morning, same job.

variants.title: Gull squabble on the beach
variants.body: Two ring-bills, one snack, lots of opinions. The snack wins.

variants.title: Ring-billed gulls are walking the edge of {water}
variants.body: Up and down the waterline, peeking at everything the tide left behind.

variants.title: The ring-billed gulls are sleeping on the water
variants.body: Rafts of them, floating together out where it's safe. Even gulls need a quiet night.

variants.title: A floating gull slumber party
variants.body: Hundreds of gulls, bobbing on the dark water, heads tucked in.

variants.title: The gulls are asleep out on {water}
variants.body: Floating together far from shore, tucked in and quiet for once.

variants.title: A tern is dive-bombing for fish
variants.body: Hover, hover, SPLASH. They plunge headfirst after tiny fish and pop right back up.

variants.title: A tern is hovering in place
variants.body: Wings flicking, eyes locked on the water. Any second now...

variants.title: A tern is diving into {water}
variants.body: Hovering high, then straight down headfirst. A tiny splash, and up they come with a silver fish.

variants.title: A tern is bringing a fish as a gift
variants.body: He flies around showing it off, then offers it to her. Romance, tern style.

variants.title: Tern courtship is in the air
variants.body: A fish in his beak, a little parade flight. She's considering it.

variants.title: A tern is courting over {water}
variants.body: He swoops past with a fish in his beak, hoping she'll accept it.

variants.title: Tern parents are on a nonstop fish run
variants.body: Dive, catch, fly to the chicks, repeat. All day long.

variants.title: Fluffy tern chicks are waiting on the beach
variants.body: Mom and dad keep the fish coming. Everyone else should keep their distance.

variants.title: Tern parents are fishing all day off {water}
variants.body: Back and forth from the water to the chicks, one tiny fish at a time.

variants.title: The terns are heading to South America
variants.body: A long trip for a slim little seabird. They'll be back next spring.

variants.title: Last call for the terns
variants.body: A few are still diving before the big flight south.

variants.title: The last terns are leaving {water}
variants.body: One more dive, then off to South America for the winter.

variants.title: A great blue heron is standing perfectly still
variants.body: Not a statue. A very patient fisher. Watch long enough and... strike!

variants.title: A heron is fishing in slow motion
variants.body: One step. Pause. One step. Then a lightning-fast stab at a fish.

variants.title: A great blue heron is fishing at {water}
variants.body: Knee-deep in the shallows, still as a fence post, waiting for the perfect moment.

variants.title: A great blue heron is flying home
variants.body: Huge wings, slow beats, neck folded into an S, legs trailing behind. Like a tiny dinosaur.

variants.title: Big gray bird, slow wingbeats
variants.body: That's a heron heading to roost. Graceful, a little prehistoric.

variants.title: A heron is flapping slowly over {water}
variants.body: Neck tucked, legs trailing, heading home for the night.

variants.title: A heron is hunched by open water
variants.body: Neck pulled in, feathers fluffed. Winter fishing takes patience.

variants.title: A heron stayed for winter
variants.body: Not all herons fly south. This one is waiting by the open water.

variants.title: A heron is waiting out the cold by {water}
variants.body: Hunched and fluffed up at the water's edge, still fishing.

variants.title: The night herons are clocking in
variants.body: As everyone else heads to bed, they wake up, stretch, and head for the water.

variants.title: A night heron just woke up
variants.body: Red eyes open, a big stretch, and off to work. Their shift starts at sundown.

variants.title: Night herons are heading out to {water}
variants.body: As the light fades, they leave their daytime trees and settle in at the water's edge to fish.

variants.title: A night heron is fishing in the dark
variants.body: Hunched, still, red eyes watching the water. Very spooky, very cute.

variants.title: Night shift at the water's edge
variants.body: A stocky little heron with a black cap is waiting for something to swim by.

variants.title: A night heron is fishing along {water}
variants.body: Under the streetlights and the moon, waiting patiently at the edge.

variants.title: Night herons are napping in the trees
variants.body: By day they doze on branches over the water, hunched up like little gray loaves.

variants.title: Shh, the night herons are sleeping
variants.body: They worked all night. Let them nap.

variants.title: Night herons are dozing in the trees near {water}
variants.body: A row of hunched little herons on a branch, catching up on sleep.

variants.title: Buffleheads are playing hide and seek
variants.body: Dive, vanish, pop up somewhere else. They're tiny ducks with a lot of energy.

variants.title: A bufflehead is bobbing like a bath toy
variants.body: Little black-and-white duck, big white head patch, back underwater in three, two, one.

variants.title: Buffleheads are diving out on {water}
variants.body: A little flock keeps vanishing and popping back up, white head patches flashing.

variants.title: The buffleheads are back for the winter
variants.body: Tiny diving ducks, fresh in from the forests of Canada.

variants.title: Winter ducks have arrived
variants.body: Little black-and-white buffleheads are back on the water.

variants.title: Buffleheads have arrived on {water}
variants.body: Fresh from northern forests, they'll be diving here all winter.

variants.title: The buffleheads are tucked in on the water
variants.body: A small raft, floating together, heads tucked back for the night.

variants.title: Buffleheads are drifting off to sleep
variants.body: Bobbing in a little group, close together, out on the dark water.

variants.title: Buffleheads are resting on {water}
variants.body: Floating together in a tight little raft for the night.

variants.title: A swan is gliding across the pond
variants.body: Neck in a perfect S, barely a ripple. Under the water, the feet are working hard.

variants.title: A swan is preening very carefully
variants.body: Every feather, one at a time. Looking that elegant takes work.

variants.title: A mute swan is gliding on {water}
variants.body: Slow and graceful, neck curved, leaving a long soft wake behind.

variants.title: A swan is sitting on a giant nest
variants.body: A huge pile of reeds at the water's edge. Their partner patrols nearby. Give them lots of room.

variants.title: Swan on guard duty
variants.body: Wings slightly raised, watching everyone. They're protecting their eggs.

variants.title: A swan is guarding a nest by {water}
variants.body: A big mound of reeds at the edge, and a very watchful swan on top.

variants.title: Swan cygnets are riding on a parent's back
variants.body: Fluffy and gray, tucked between the wings, cruising across the pond in style.

variants.title: A swan family is out for a paddle
variants.body: Two big white parents, a row of fuzzy gray cygnets. Picture perfect.

variants.title: A swan family is paddling on {water}
variants.body: Fluffy gray cygnets following their parents in a little line.

variants.title: Whoosh, whoosh, a swan is flying past
variants.body: Their wings make a loud, rhythmic hum. You can hear them before you see them.

variants.title: A mute swan is taking off
variants.body: A long running start across the water, then big, loud, whooshing wings.

variants.title: A swan is flying low over {water}
variants.body: Listen for the whoosh of those big wings.

variants.title: A red-winged blackbird is shouting conk-la-ree
variants.body: Shoulders puffed, red patches flashing, perched on top of a cattail. Spring is officially here.

variants.title: Conk-la-ree! from the cattails
variants.body: A male is singing his heart out, showing off his red shoulders.

variants.title: A red-winged blackbird is singing by {water}
variants.body: Perched on a cattail, red shoulders flashing, announcing spring to everyone nearby.

variants.title: The red-winged blackbirds are back
variants.body: Among the very first birds of spring, here to claim the best cattails.

variants.title: First sign of spring: conk-la-ree
variants.body: The blackbirds are back and very loud about it.

variants.title: Red-winged blackbirds just arrived at {water}
variants.body: Early spring, and they're already claiming their cattails.

variants.title: A cloud of blackbirds is swirling overhead
variants.body: Hundreds flying together before heading south.

variants.title: Blackbird flocks are gathering
variants.body: Red-wings, grackles and starlings mixing together in big, noisy flocks.

variants.title: Blackbirds are swirling over {green}
variants.body: A big noisy flock, gathering up before the trip south.

variants.title: A deer is stepping out of the trees
variants.body: Ears forward, nose working, one slow step at a time. Dawn and dusk are their favorite hours.

variants.title: A deer is nibbling at the edge of the woods
variants.body: Big ears turning like satellite dishes, listening to everything.

variants.title: A deer is grazing at the edge of {green}
variants.body: Quiet and careful, just inside the trees, ears turning toward every sound.

variants.title: A spotted fawn is hiding in the tall grass
variants.body: Mom is nearby eating. The fawn stays perfectly still and almost scent-free. If you see one, smile and walk away.

variants.title: A deer mom and her fawn are out together
variants.body: The fawn wobbles after her on very long legs, white spots and all.

variants.title: A deer mom is feeding near {green}
variants.body: Her spotted fawn is tucked away nearby in the tall grass, waiting perfectly still for her to come back.

variants.title: A deer just flipped up their white tail
variants.body: That white flag says: something startled me, I'm out of here. Bound, bound, gone.

variants.title: White tails bouncing into the woods
variants.body: A little group of deer, startled by something, bounding away with tails up.

variants.title: A deer is bounding back into the trees near {green}
variants.body: White tail up like a flag, three big leaps, and gone.

variants.title: A deer is munching acorns
variants.body: Fall is snack season. Bucks have their antlers, and everyone is bulking up for winter.

variants.title: A buck with new antlers is out
variants.body: He's careful and quiet, nibbling acorns under the oaks.

variants.title: Deer are eating acorns near {green}
variants.body: Fall means acorns, and a few deer are making the most of them.

variants.title: A mockingbird is singing a medley
variants.body: A robin, a cardinal, a car alarm, a squeaky gate, all in one breath. Each song gets repeated a few times before the next.

variants.title: The neighborhood DJ is on
variants.body: Twenty different songs and counting, from the top of an antenna. No two minutes sound the same.

variants.title: A mockingbird is performing above {street}
variants.body: From the highest antenna around, they're running through every song they've ever heard, including a few car alarms.

variants.title: A mockingbird is singing in the middle of the night
variants.body: Unpaired males sometimes sing all night long, especially under bright city lights. Very romantic. Very loud.

variants.title: Someone's singing under the streetlight
variants.body: That's a mockingbird, still going at midnight, hoping someone special is listening.

variants.title: A mockingbird is serenading {street} at midnight
variants.body: Under the streetlights, a lonely male is singing song after song, hoping to impress.

variants.title: A mockingbird is guarding a berry bush
variants.body: This bush is theirs for the winter. Any robin who tries for a snack gets chased off.

variants.title: Mockingbird flashing their wings
variants.body: They lift their wings to show white patches. Maybe to startle bugs, maybe just to show off.

variants.title: A mockingbird is defending a berry bush near {green}
variants.body: All winter long, this one bush is theirs, and they'll chase off anyone who tries a berry.

variants.title: A cardinal is feeding his partner
variants.body: He hops over, a seed in his beak, and passes it to her beak to beak. It's basically a kiss.

variants.title: Cardinal couple goals
variants.body: He brings her snacks, she sings back from the nest. They're together all year.

variants.title: A cardinal couple is sharing snacks near {green}
variants.body: He picks a seed and hands it to her beak to beak, right there in the hedge.

variants.title: A red cardinal is glowing in the hedge
variants.body: Bright red against the gray, puffed up round, checking for seeds.

variants.title: A cardinal is fluffed up like a red tomato
variants.body: Feathers puffed out to stay warm. Very round, very red.

variants.title: A cardinal is visiting the hedges along {street}
variants.body: A flash of red in the bare branches, round and puffed up against the cold.

variants.title: A cardinal is whistling cheer, cheer, cheer
variants.body: Loud and clear from the top of a tree. Often the female sings back.

variants.title: Birdie, birdie, birdie
variants.body: That's a cardinal, whistling from the treetop at first light.

variants.title: A cardinal is whistling over {street}
variants.body: Cheer, cheer, cheer, loud and bright, as the neighborhood wakes up.

variants.title: The cardinals are the last ones at the snack bar
variants.body: Cardinals often feed late, right as the light is fading.

variants.title: A cardinal is calling chip, chip in the dusk
variants.body: One last check-in with their partner before bed.

variants.title: Cardinals are grabbing a late snack near {green}
variants.body: They're often the last birds out as the light fades.

variants.title: A grackle is strutting across the lawn
variants.body: Long tail held in a V, yellow eyes on the grass. Very serious walk.

variants.title: The grackles are shining in the sun
variants.body: Black at first glance, then purple, blue and bronze when the light hits.

variants.title: A grackle is strutting near {green}
variants.body: Shiny and serious, tail in a V, marching across the grass looking for bugs.

variants.title: A grackle is singing like a rusty gate
variants.body: Puffs up, fluffs out, and makes a sound like squeaky hinges. He thinks it's beautiful.

variants.title: Squeak, creak, that's a grackle
variants.body: The rusty-gate song is how male grackles show off.

variants.title: A grackle is squeaking from a tree over {street}
variants.body: Puffed up, tail spread, singing his rusty-gate song with total confidence.

variants.title: Huge flocks of grackles are heading to roost
variants.body: Thousands, mixed with starlings and red-wings, streaming across the evening sky.

variants.title: A river of blackbirds overhead
variants.body: Fall flocks of grackles can be enormous and very noisy.

variants.title: Grackles are streaming over {green}
variants.body: A long noisy river of blackbirds, all heading to the same roost.

variants.title: A catbird just meowed at you
variants.body: Not a kitten. A slim gray bird hiding in the bush, making a perfect cat sound.

variants.title: Mew, says the bushes
variants.body: That's a catbird. They meow, then launch into a long rambling song.

variants.title: A catbird is meowing from the shrubs near {green}
variants.body: Somewhere in there is a slim gray bird with a black cap, sounding exactly like a cat.

variants.title: A catbird is gobbling berries
variants.body: Fueling up for the trip south. Every berry counts.

variants.title: Catbird snack time
variants.body: Hopping through the branches, picking the ripest berries one by one.

variants.title: A catbird is eating berries near {green}
variants.body: Getting ready for a long trip south, one ripe berry at a time.

variants.title: A catbird is rambling on and on
variants.body: Squeaks, whistles, chatters, borrowed sounds, all jumbled together for minutes.

variants.title: Catbird open mic night
variants.body: A long improvised song from deep inside the bushes.

variants.title: A catbird is singing in the bushes along {street}
variants.body: A long, jumbly, improvised song, right as the evening settles in.

variants.title: A song sparrow is singing on a sunny day
variants.body: Even in winter, a bit of sun gets them going. Three clear notes, then a jumble.

variants.title: Song sparrow on the top of a shrub
variants.body: Head back, beak open, singing their neighborhood's local tune.

variants.title: A song sparrow is singing by {water}
variants.body: Perched on a low shrub, singing the local song all the neighbors know.

variants.title: A song sparrow is pumping their tail
variants.body: When they fly a short way, their tail pumps up and down. That's how you know it's them.

variants.title: A streaky sparrow with a dark spot
variants.body: That spot in the middle of the chest is the song sparrow's badge.

variants.title: A song sparrow is hopping along the edge of {green}
variants.body: Streaky brown, dark chest spot, tail pumping as they flit from weed to weed.

variants.title: A song sparrow is tucking into the tangles
variants.body: Low in a thick shrub, safe and snug for the night.

variants.title: Lights out for the song sparrow
variants.body: Deep in the brambles, feathers fluffed, done singing for today.

variants.title: A song sparrow is settling in near {water}
variants.body: Low in a tangled shrub, tucked away for the night.

variants.title: A kestrel is hovering in midair
variants.body: Wings fluttering, tail spread, head perfectly still. Then down onto a grasshopper.

variants.title: A tiny falcon is hanging in the sky
variants.body: Kestrels can hover in place like a helicopter, watching the ground.

variants.title: A kestrel is hovering over {green}
variants.body: Wings a blur, head perfectly still, staring down at the grass.

variants.title: A kestrel is perched on a wire
variants.body: Small and colorful, bobbing their tail, eyes on the ground below.

variants.title: The smallest falcon is watching the street
variants.body: A kestrel on a wire, as colorful as a parrot and as focused as a hawk.

variants.title: A kestrel is watching from a wire along {street}
variants.body: Tail bobbing, head turning, waiting for something to move in the grass.

variants.title: Kestrels are nesting in an old building
variants.body: They use nooks in cornices and walls, right in the middle of the city.

variants.title: A kestrel is bringing home a grasshopper
variants.body: Somewhere in a gap in the building, hungry chicks are waiting.

variants.title: Kestrels are nesting in a nook near {landmark}
variants.body: A gap in old brickwork makes a perfect falcon home.

variants.title: A Cooper's hawk just zipped through the trees
variants.body: Fast, low, and gone. Every small bird nearby froze.

variants.title: All the little birds just went quiet
variants.body: There's probably a Cooper's hawk perched nearby, very still.

variants.title: A Cooper's hawk is darting through the trees near {green}
variants.body: A flash of striped tail between the branches, and every small bird hides.

variants.title: A Cooper's hawk is sitting very still in a tree
variants.body: Red eyes, barred orange chest, long striped tail. Patient and focused.

variants.title: A hawk is hiding in plain sight
variants.body: Cooper's hawks often perch inside a tree, not on top, so they can surprise their prey.

variants.title: A Cooper's hawk is perched in the trees near {green}
variants.body: Tucked inside the branches, watching everything below.

variants.title: A Cooper's hawk family is up in the tree
variants.body: Fluffy white chicks peek over the edge of a stick nest, waiting for dinner.

variants.title: Hawk parents on duty
variants.body: One guards the nest while the other hunts.

variants.title: Cooper's hawks are nesting in a tall tree near {green}
variants.body: High up, a stick nest, and fluffy white chicks waiting for lunch.

variants.title: A peregrine is diving at top speed
variants.body: Wings tucked, over 200 miles an hour. The fastest animal on Earth, right overhead.

variants.title: A falcon just stooped past
variants.body: That blur was a peregrine diving after a pigeon. The pigeon usually wins, honestly.

variants.title: A peregrine is diving over {street}
variants.body: From high above, wings folded, faster than anything else alive.

variants.title: A peregrine is perched on a high ledge
variants.body: Dark helmet, sharp eyes, scanning the sky from the city's cliffs.

variants.title: The falcons are home on the bridge
variants.body: Bridges and skyscrapers are perfect cliffs for peregrines.

variants.title: A peregrine is perched high above {street}
variants.body: On a tall ledge, dark helmet, watching the whole neighborhood.

variants.title: Peregrine chicks are on a skyscraper ledge
variants.body: Fluffy white balls of down, high above the street, waiting for their next meal.

variants.title: Young peregrines are learning to fly
variants.body: Clumsy first flights between rooftops, with parents watching closely.

variants.title: Peregrines are raising chicks high above {street}
variants.body: On a bare stone ledge, fluffy white chicks wait for their parents to come back.

variants.title: A downy woodpecker is tapping for bugs
variants.body: Tap, tap, tap. Tiny, black and white, hitching up the trunk in little hops.

variants.title: A little drummer is at work
variants.body: Soft taps on bark mean a downy is looking for a snack.

variants.title: A downy woodpecker is tapping on a tree near {green}
variants.body: Small and busy, hopping up the trunk, tapping for bugs under the bark.

variants.title: A woodpecker is drumming a rhythm
variants.body: Fast rat-a-tat on a hollow branch. It's how downies say hello, or hey, this is mine.

variants.title: Rat-a-tat-tat from the treetops
variants.body: That's not construction. That's a downy woodpecker drumming.

variants.title: A downy is drumming in the trees near {green}
variants.body: A quick rat-a-tat on a hollow branch, echoing across the neighborhood.

variants.title: A downy woodpecker is asleep in a tree hole
variants.body: Tucked inside a hole they carved themselves, safe from the cold.

variants.title: Woodpecker bedtime
variants.body: Each downy sleeps alone in their own little tree hole.

variants.title: A downy woodpecker is sleeping in a tree near {green}
variants.body: Snug inside a little hole in a dead branch, out of the wind.

variants.title: A red-bellied woodpecker is calling kwirr
variants.body: That loud, rolling call echoes across the park. Look for zebra stripes on the trunk.

variants.title: Kwirr, kwirr, says the woodpecker
